title: Agentic Deployment x Static Pre-Deployment Evals: The Capability a One-Shot Eval Can't See

original_idea.body:
# Agentic Deployment x Static Pre-Deployment Evals: The Capability a One-Shot Eval Can't See

**Problem:** Governance certifies models with static single-turn evals; agentic deployment composes capabilities over steps producing emergent dangerous behavior.

**Direction:** On a small open model, compare single-turn score vs success with a multi-step scaffold/tool loop on the same goal; quantify the uplift; recommend an agentic-scaffold allowance.

**Why it matters:** Shows a structural gap between certification and deployment. Single GPU, public model.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2506.04018; arXiv:2507.16534; arXiv:2407.14981.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: certification underestimates deployed-agent capability, a recognized critical pathway; concrete uplift deliverable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Single-turn vs simple scaffold comparison on one open model; guided and tractable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped uplift measurement with clear success criterion.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open model, medium-horizon threat labs underweight; cheap scaffolding.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference with a scaffold loop on a small open model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Agentic-scaffold uplift is studied; the certification-allowance framing may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Scaffolding uplift is documented; the governance certification-gap framing may be open.
